boundary_metadata.scope: read_chunk return includes server wait, IPC and C++ Arrow decoding; post_chunk_python covers Python log validation/event construction; no payload decoding before the benchmark received timestamp
boundary_metadata.overhead: two clock reads plus dictionary insertion per sampled event; method wrapping and modulo checks each event; output after consumption

interpretation_limits: sent to read_chunk return includes server processing/wait, local transport, and client C++ Arrow decoding. It is not an observed server-send timestamp.
read_chunk to next return isolates the Python log metadata validation/event construction suffix. Flat values exclude growth only in that measured suffix.
Use Catalog/file/lineage/snapshot/segment counts and server CPU/RSS alongside code evidence before attributing upstream growth to the server.
Boundary samples are one event per sample_every rows; sparse per-minute p99 is descriptive and cannot replace the full benchmark p99 acceptance test.
Minute origin/warmup matches the original benchmark. Partial final minutes are displayed but excluded from signed OLS slopes and first/last ratios.
Resource points have their actual timestamps, including negative startup offsets. CPU per 60 seconds is a normalization over observed intervals, not exact minute data.
RSS for writer/subscriber includes retained raw sample integer lists, which grow linearly with sample count; increasing RSS alone does not establish a leak.
Catalog counters are independent read-only index queries with a 50 ms progress budget, not an atomic cross-table snapshot. Errors and incomplete walks are retained.
Sampling wraps both reader methods on every event; sampled events add two clock reads and a dictionary insertion. Main sample values and thresholds are unchanged.
